HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Wide worm's-eye shot from the grass of a bare mountain ridge in the far north, storm sky in granulated watercolor filling the upper half, one cloud-break shaft falling on the stone. A tall rough granite boundary stele, its face still BLANK weathered stone with only chisel scars and lichen, NO characters, NO writing of any kind, stands on the ridge line as the one vertical device. King Jinheung, thirty-four, in red silk travelling robe and gold crown, cloak whipping in the wind, one hand flat on the stone, looks down at a wiry commoner mason in undyed white hemp who argues up at him, a small iron chisel in one fist and a wooden mallet in the other. Two tiny spear guards far down the slope dissolving in haze. Dry grass bending. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = jinheung. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. KING JINHEUNG — Crown: Silla gold crown: a gold band with three stepped tree-branch uprights and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. Colour #2f6fd4. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
